text: A developer's in-progress model and the business's trusted numbers need to coexist without colliding. This lesson builds the schema structure that makes that possible: RAW, DEV, and PROD.

RAW is untouched source data. DEV is where a developer's dbt build lands while they're actively working — safe to be wrong or half-finished. PROD is the one schema that has already passed Chapter 4's tests and Chapter 6's CI gate.

TRANSFORMER gets full access to DEV and PROD, since dbt itself writes to both. ANALYST only ever reads PROD — including a future-tables grant, so a newly built mart is automatically readable without a manual re-grant every time.

dbt doesn't know dev and prod as a built-in concept — it knows targets, named connection profiles. This platform defines a dev target and a prod target, each pointing dbt build at a different real Snowflake schema.

A real team often goes one step further, giving each developer a personal schema like dev_alice, so two people building at once never collide. Next: the actual profiles.yml file that makes this dev-versus-prod split real for a team.
